1. Failing to document your setup—because why would anyone need to know how you do it?
2. Ignoring updates—because fresh pain doesn't matter if it's not yours.
3. Overcomplicating the configuration—because more complexity means more blame.
4. Underestimating security—because why would you want intruders peeking at your cat videos?
5. Mislabeling network cables—because nobody gets fired for buying too many patch cords.
6. Not having a backup strategy—because losing data is just part of the adventure.
7. Believing in magic

1. Lack of documentation—because who has time to write things down?
2. Overconfidence in your setup—until the inevitable fails.
3. Ignoring security updates—until you wish you hadn't.
4. Not testing backups—until you need them.
5. Using default passwords—because "admin" is just so obvious.
6. Buying the cheapest hardware—until you can't afford the downtime.
7. Not having a plan B—because when things go south, they go fast.
